subject: Private offer negotiation: true-up cadence, list-price mirroring & partner surcharge
messages:
From: Sanjay Gupta <sanjay@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private offer ask: commit sizing, surcharge handling, true-up cadence

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're preparing a Private Offer request for Redwood across our developer accounts in US-East and US-West. High-level ask:

- Target commit: $250,000 ARR (usage-based PO)
- Term: looking at 12 months but open to discussion
- Channel: we'll resell to our customers and need a fair reseller margin; our finance team expects ~12% pass-through margin on list prices
- Marketplace behavior: we want marketplace list-price mirroring where feasible so our ordering systems don't have to handle netting logic
- True-up cadence: would prefer monthly true-up for finance accuracy but can consider quarterly if there are platform constraints

Two specific questions for Redwood:
1) Can you mirror list prices in the marketplace and let us apply our reseller margin on top, or do you require surcharge to be baked into list price?
2) How are true-ups typically handled for private offers (monthly vs quarterly vs invoice adjustments)?

I've attached our estimated usage workbook for reference.

Cheers,
Sanjay
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Corp
[Attachment: ACME_commit_workbook.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Gupta <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer ask: commit sizing, surcharge handling, true-up cadence

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the workbook and the clear summary. Looping in Ben (sales ops) and Irene (channel/ops) to confirm mechanics. Quick take from product/sales: we can run two high-level paths for a Private Offer:

Option A — List-price mirroring + surcharge handled by Acme:
- Redwood lists a SKU at a standard public list price in the marketplace
- Partner (Acme) invoices end customers at list price + your reseller uplift externally or handles margin in your downstream billing
- NOTE: on some market marketplaces (AWS), marketplace private-offer flows don’t allow a separate line-item surcharge from Redwood; that surcharge would need to be represented in your invoice or built into a partner-managed price layer

Option B — Net pricing on private offer (Redwood sets net price to Acme and Redwood records partner margin pass-through):
- Redwood offers a net effective price to Acme (private offer), and Acme lists your own price to end customers
- We can do a reseller credit flow so your 12% margin is realized as a credit on Redwood invoices to Acme

Operationally we usually see quarterly true-ups for Private Offers to reduce invoice churn, but Ben/Irene can confirm if monthly is viable.

Ben/Irene — can you review the attached workbook and advise on: 1) whether we can support list-price mirroring for the requested SKUs, 2) how a 12% pass-through vs a built-in surcharge would map to our billing and marketplace constraints, and 3) the preferred true-up cadence from an ops standpoint?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call this week to walk through options.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of GTM (Marketplace Partnerships)
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sanjay Gupta <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private offer ask: commit sizing, surcharge handling, true-up cadence

Sanjay / team — I pulled the workbook and modeled two scenarios. Attaching the quick calc.

Notes:
- Standard starting position: Redwood's default reseller uplift for marketplace/private-offer flows is 15% (this covers distributor/marketplace fees and margin).
- We can accommodate 12% net yield to Acme if the commit is >= $200k and the term is >= 12 months (so the $250k ask qualifies). This would be implemented as a net pricing proposal to Acme (Option B from Marcus) where Redwood invoices Acme at the net price; Acme lists whatever price to end customers.
- Mechanic for pass-through: we prefer a reseller credit approach on our invoice rather than separate marketplace line-item surcharges because:
   - Some marketplaces don’t expose flexible surcharge lines and will complicate tax handling.
   - Credit/invoice flow keeps Redwood revenue recognition clean and allows us to show a partner-credit line on your monthly invoice.
- If Acme strongly prefers list-price mirroring in the marketplace (Option A), the partner surcharge would have to be handled client-side (your billing) — Redwood can't create an extra marketplace line item on AWS Private Offers. For GCP/Azure there are similar constraints; implementation varies by provider.

Tax and compliance catch: if we do net invoicing + partner credit, we need to confirm whether Acme is a reseller (resale) or an agent for tax treatment — please confirm your company legal/contact.

See attachment: partner_margin_calc.csv — shows revenue to Redwood, credit line to Acme, and implied list price if you want us to propose an MSRP.

Ben
Sr. Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: partner_margin_calc.csv (csv)]

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sanjay Gupta <sanjay@acme.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private offer ask: commit sizing, surcharge handling, true-up cadence

Operational constraints from marketplace/channel side (summarized):

- True-up cadence: monthly consolidated true-ups are possible but increase operational noise and risk (more invoice adjustments, higher support overhead). Our recommended default is quarterly true-ups aligned with invoice cycles — this reduces churn and simplifies reconciliation for both parties.
- Marketplace-specific notes:
  - AWS Private Offers: vendor (Redwood) cannot add a separate surcharge line item at purchase time for a partner; any uplift needs to be managed by the reseller (Acme) downstream, or baked into the list price on the Marketplace SKU (which would then be visible to all buyers).
  - GCP & Azure: similar constraints; Azure has slightly more flexibility around reseller billing but still prefers net pricing + partner-managed downstream pricing for clean invoicing.
- Implementation path we recommend for this deal (to meet Acme's 12% margin ask):
  1) Redwood issues a private-offer net price to Acme that effectively embeds the partner credit mechanism (so Acme receives a monthly credit equal to 12% of list-side ARR).
  2) We run quarterly true-ups to reconcile actual usage vs commit and apply an adjustment credit/debit on Redwood's invoice to Acme.
  3) DocuSign MOU to capture the credit mechanics and commit tiers; ops will require reseller tax form and billing contact.

Action items for Acme: please confirm:
- legal entity for billing (resale vs. agent),
- acceptance of quarterly true-up cadence, and
- commitment to a 12-month term if you want the 12% effective margin.

I'll attach a short ops note with required artifacts.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Channel Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops_notes.md (text)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Gupta <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer ask: commit sizing, surcharge handling, true-up cadence — next steps

Sanjay — thanks for the quick responses. To summarize and propose next steps:

- We will accommodate a 12% effective reseller margin for Acme provided the deal is a 12-month term and commit is $250k ARR (meets thresholds).
- Mechanic: Redwood will issue a net private offer to Acme and apply a partner credit equal to 12% of list-equivalent usage on our invoices (quarterly true-up cadence to reconcile actuals).
- Marketplace list-price mirroring: not guaranteed across all clouds. For AWS, surcharge cannot be a separate Redwood line item — you will need to handle downstream list price display if exact marketplace MSRP mirroring is critical. We can provide recommended MSRP guidance in the PO if helpful.

Next steps:
1) If Acme agrees: I will circulate an MOU via DocuSign capturing the commit, term, margin credit mechanics, and the quarterly true-up cadence.
2) Irene will send required ops artifact checklist (tax forms, billing contact, reseller certification).
3) Ben will share the finalized pricing table for the marketplace SKUs so you can mirror the list price if you choose that route.

Sanjay — can you confirm by EOD tomorrow if Acme accepts the 12-month term and quarterly true-ups? If yes, I’ll start the DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of GTM (Marketplace Partnerships)
Redwood Inference
[DocuSign request: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-acme-mou]
